claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified now on a narrow aggregate-readiness basis despite a known gap in the health-plan benefits support segment, with ongoing monitoring and documentation handling the remaining risk.
decision_criteria: Verdict would improve if admissible evidence showed the gap was disclosed as required before launch.
Verdict would improve if admissible evidence showed approved risk acceptance for the unresolved material limitation.
Verdict would improve if legal or policy evidence definitively established that this segment is not material under the stated policy.
Verdict would worsen to noncompliant if evidence showed launch proceeded without disclosure or approved risk acceptance despite the unresolved named-segment gap.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the health-plan benefits support gap must be disclosed for this launch.
Evidence that the limitation has already been disclosed in the model card or other required launch materials.
Approved risk-acceptance record, if the team intends to launch before the gap is resolved.
Decision record establishing whether the regulated-customer pilot order form makes this a named launch use case or contractual customer segment under policy.
specific_concerns: The evidence supports aggregate readiness, but aggregate readiness does not resolve the policy requirement for material limitations affecting named launch use cases or contractual customer segments.
The health-plan benefits support segment is below target and is named in a regulated-customer pilot order form, which is direct evidence of possible materiality under the stated policy text.
There is no admissible evidence that the limitation was disclosed before launch.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance covering the unresolved gap.
Legal review is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved at decision time.
Public guidance about monitoring and model-card documentation supports governance process, but it does not itself authorize certification when a release-policy disclosure condition may be unmet.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify_model is not fully supported because the record does not show the named-segment limitation was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
The implication that ongoing monitoring and documentation are sufficient to cure the current policy issue is unsupported by the admissible evidence.
Any conclusion that the named-segment gap is non-material is unsupported given the contractual reference and pending legal review.
